newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE accuses Israel of Internet disinformation.
newsitem.headline: UAE accuses Israel of Internet disinformation.

text.p: A United Arab Emirates police chief accused Israel of launching a disinformation campaign on the Internet, saying the Jewish state was trying to portray itself as a peaceful country on the global computer web.
"Israel is now trying to portray itself as a peace-loving nation through the Internet," Dubai Police Chief Dhahi Khalfan Tamim told the English-language Khaleej Times.
He also expressed concern that UAE nationals and other Arabs could chat with Israelis over the information super-highway.

"Computer-users in the UAE and other Arab states can chat with Israelis on the Internet and exchange important information," he said on the sidelines of an information seminar in the UAE capital Abu Dhabi.
The UAE, a conservative Gulf Arab state in which newspapers, magazines, books and films are censored, is also anxious about the spread of pornography over web sites.

Tamim said the UAE telecommunications giant Etisalat, which provides access to the Internet, had launched a new plan to combat pornography and other "undesirable material" on the rapidly growing computer web.

"As more computer users are linking up to Internet in the UAE, the spread of undesirable material among the country's youths will become more visible. This will require the intervention of the authorities," he said.
Etisalat has said it would disconnect any customers who abused Internet services and violated "order and clear laws" of the UAE.
